source_refs.note: Practice long questions written from Unit 7 (PDF 220-233, printed 218-231); not printed in the book. Based on the unit's text, theorems, formulas and worked examples (changed values); none repeats the unit's exercises. Drafts needing academic review.

blocks.text: Practice long questions for the whole of Unit 7 (Kinematics of Motion in a Straight Line (TOC: 'Kinematics')), in the shape of a Board Section-II question part: each carries 5 marks (a longer problem, a proof or a derivation). Each one is solved in full, step by step.

blocks.prompt: 1 A particle moves along a straight line with \(x(t) = t^{3} - 9t^{2} + 24t\) (\(x\) in m, \(t\) in s), \(0 \le t \le 5\). Find (i) its velocity and acceleration (ii) when it is at rest (iii) its displacement and the distance travelled in the \(5\) s (iv) its average speed. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Differentiate for \(v\) and \(a\); the particle turns back where \(v = 0\), so add the pieces of path between the turning points.

book_ref.quote: Average velocity uses displacement, so it can be negative or zero.

steps: \(v = 0\) at \(t = 2\) s and \(t = 4\) s (momentarily at rest)

blocks.prompt: 2 Prove that \(a = v\dfrac{dv}{dx}\) when \(v\) is a function of the displacement \(x\). Hence show that a particle whose velocity is \(v = \sqrt{9 + 4x}\) moves with constant acceleration, and find its velocity when \(x = 4\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Chain rule through \(x\); then apply the formula to the given \(v(x)\).

book_ref.quote: If velocity \(v\) of the particle is given as a function of displacement \(x\): Using the Chain Rule:

steps: \(a = \dfrac{dv}{dt} = \dfrac{dv}{dx} \cdot \dfrac{dx}{dt}\) (chain rule, since \(v\) depends on \(x\) and \(x\) on \(t\))
blocks.final_answer: Hence proved: \(a = v\dfrac{dv}{dx}\); here \(a = 2\) (constant) and \(v = 5\) when \(x = 4\).

blocks.prompt: 3 The position of a particle is \(x(t) = 2t^{3} - 21t^{2} + 60t\) (m, s). Find its velocity and acceleration at \(t = 1\), \(t = 3\) and \(t = 6\) s, and say each time in which direction it moves and whether it is speeding up or slowing down. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: The sign of \(v\) gives the direction; same signs of \(v\) and \(a\) mean speeding up, opposite signs slowing down.

book_ref.quote: At \(t = 1\) both \(v\) and \(a\) are negative (same sign), so the particle is speeding up in the negative direction.

steps: \(t = 1\): \(v = 24\) m/s, \(a = -30\) m/s\(^{2}\): positive direction, opposite signs, slowing down
\(t = 3\): \(v = -12\) m/s, \(a = -6\) m/s\(^{2}\): negative direction, same signs, speeding up
\(t = 6\): \(v = 24\) m/s, \(a = 30\) m/s\(^{2}\): positive direction, same signs, speeding up

blocks.prompt: 4 A delivery rider's displacement-time graph joins \(O(0, 0)\), \(A(15, 6)\), \(B(25, 6)\), \(C(45, 10)\) and \(D(60, 0)\) by straight lines (\(t\) in minutes, \(x\) in km). Find (i) the velocity on each stage in km/h (ii) the average velocity and (iii) the average speed for the whole journey. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Velocity on a stage is the slope; convert km/min to km/h by multiplying by 60; the waiting time counts.

book_ref.quote: They help us easily determine whether an object is moving, stationary or accelerating.

steps: Total displacement \(= 0\) (D is on the time axis), so average velocity \(= \dfrac{0}{1} = 0\) km/h
Distance \(= 6 + 0 + 4 + 10 = 20\) km in \(60\) min \(= 1\) h: average speed \(= 20\) km/h

blocks.prompt: 5 A family drives from home for \(1.5\) h at an average velocity of \(80\) km/h (point \(A\)), stops for \(0.5\) h (to point \(B\)) and then drives on in the same direction for \(1\) h to point \(C\). On the displacement-time graph \(A\) is \(8\) grid units above the time axis and \(C\) is \(11\) units above it. Find (i) the displacement of \(C\) from home (ii) the velocity during the last hour (iii) the average velocity for the whole journey. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: The first drive gives the displacement at A, which fixes the scale of the vertical axis.

book_ref.quote: That known value fixes the scale of the vertical axis, and the scale gives the rise from B to C.

steps: Scale: \(8\) units \(= 120\) km, so \(1\) unit \(= 15\) km
Rise from \(B\) to \(C = 11 - 8 = 3\) units \(= 45\) km; displacement of \(C = 120 + 45 = 165\) km
Velocity in the last hour \(= \dfrac{45}{1} = 45\) km/h
Total time \(= 1.5 + 0.5 + 1 = 3\) h; average velocity \(= \dfrac{165}{3} = 55\) km/h

blocks.prompt: 6 A car starts from rest and accelerates uniformly to \(18\) m/s in \(6\) s. It keeps this velocity for \(10\) s and then slows down uniformly, coming to rest in \(4\) s. Sketch the velocity-time graph in words and find (i) the acceleration in the first and in the last stage (ii) the total displacement (iii) the average velocity. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Accelerations are slopes; the displacement is the trapezium area under the graph.

book_ref.quote: Study motion in different time intervals clearly and effectively

steps: Graph: straight line from \((0, 0)\) to \((6, 18)\), horizontal to \((16, 18)\), straight line down to \((20, 0)\)
Parallel sides: \(20\) s (base) and \(16 - 6 = 10\) s (top); height \(18\) m/s

blocks.prompt: 7 A car travels \(95\) km along a straight road. It starts with velocity \(u\) km/h, accelerates uniformly to \(60\) km/h in \(\frac{1}{2}\) h, keeps \(60\) km/h for \(1\) h and then slows down uniformly to rest in \(\frac{1}{4}\) h. Find (i) \(u\) (ii) the acceleration in the first half hour (iii) the retardation at the end. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Displacement = area under the graph; split it at \(t = \frac{1}{2}\) into two trapeziums and solve for \(u\).

book_ref.quote: Break the region into rectangles, triangles and trapeziums

steps: First trapezium (parallel sides \(u\) and \(60\), width \(\frac{1}{2}\)): area \(= \frac{1}{2}(u + 60) \times \frac{1}{2} = \frac{u + 60}{4}\)
Second trapezium (parallel sides \(1\) and \(1.25\), height \(60\)): area \(= \frac{1}{2}(1 + 1.25) \times 60 = 67.5\)
Last stage: slope \(= \dfrac{0 - 60}{1/4} = -240\) km/h\(^{2}\), a retardation of \(240\) km/h\(^{2}\)

blocks.prompt: 8 A velocity-time graph joins \((0, 0)\), \((2, 8)\), \((5, 8)\) and \((8, -4)\) by straight lines (\(t\) in s, \(v\) in m/s). Find (i) when the particle changes its direction of motion (ii) the displacement and (iii) the distance travelled in the \(8\) s. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Direction changes where \(v\) changes sign; above-axis area minus below-axis area is displacement, their sum is distance.

book_ref.quote: Distance moved backwards cancels part of the forward distance in the displacement

blocks.prompt: 9 The velocity of a particle is \(v(t) = t^{2} - 6t + 8\) m/s for \(0 \le t \le 5\). Find its displacement and the total distance travelled. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Displacement is the integral of \(v\); for distance split the interval where \(v\) changes sign and add the absolute values.

book_ref.quote: The integral \(\int v\,dt\) over the whole interval gives \(A_{1} - A_{2}\) automatically, because the part below the axis comes out negative.

blocks.prompt: 10 A particle moves along a straight line with constant acceleration \(a\). At \(t = 0\) it is at \(x = 0\) with velocity \(u\). Derive \(v = u + at\) and \(x = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^{2}\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Integrate \(a = \frac{dv}{dt}\), then \(v = \frac{dx}{dt}\), fixing each constant from the initial condition.

book_ref.quote: Suppose a particle moves along a straight line with constant acceleration

steps: \(\dfrac{dv}{dt} = a \Rightarrow \int dv = \int a\,dt \Rightarrow v = at + c\)
blocks.final_answer: Hence proved: \(v = u + at\) and \(x = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^{2}\).

blocks.prompt: 11 Using \(v = u + at\) and \(x = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^{2}\), prove that \(2ax = v^{2} - u^{2}\). Verify it for \(u = 3\) m/s, \(a = 2\) m/s\(^{2}\), \(t = 4\) s. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Eliminate \(t\): put \(t = \frac{v - u}{a}\) into the second equation and simplify.

book_ref.quote: By simplification, we get:

blocks.final_answer: Hence proved: \(2ax = v^{2} - u^{2}\) (both sides equal \(112\) for the given values).

blocks.prompt: 12 A car moving at \(72\) km/h is brought to rest with uniform retardation in a distance of \(40\) m. Find (i) the retardation (ii) the time taken to stop (iii) the velocity of the car after it has covered \(30\) m. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Convert to m/s first; time is not given, so use \(2ax = v^{2} - u^{2}\) first.

book_ref.quote: Which equation when? Each equation links four of the five quantities

blocks.prompt: 13 A car starts from rest with a uniform acceleration of \(2\) m/s\(^{2}\) for \(10\) s, then moves with constant velocity for \(30\) s and finally decelerates uniformly to rest in \(5\) s. Find the maximum velocity, the deceleration and the total distance. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Treat each stage separately with the equations of motion and add the distances.

book_ref.quote: To relate these quantities, we use the equations of motion.

blocks.final_answer: Maximum velocity \(20\) m/s; deceleration \(4\) m/s\(^{2}\); total distance \(750\) m.

blocks.prompt: 14 A train moving at \(10\) m/s accelerates uniformly at \(0.4\) m/s\(^{2}\) until its velocity is \(20\) m/s. Find (i) the time taken (ii) the distance covered in this time (iii) the distance covered in the last \(5\) s of this time. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: The last \(5\) s is the difference of two positions: \(x(25) - x(20)\).

book_ref.quote: Equation (2) reads: final velocity = starting velocity + (gain per second)

blocks.prompt: 15 A particle moves along a straight line with acceleration \(a(t) = 6t - 4\) m/s\(^{2}\). At \(t = 0\) it is at the origin with velocity \(3\) m/s. Find \(v(t)\) and \(x(t)\), and the velocity and position at \(t = 2\) s. Show that the particle never comes to rest. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Acceleration depends on \(t\), so integrate twice; for 'never at rest' show \(v(t) = 0\) has no real root.

book_ref.quote: If \(a\) depends on \(t\) (as in Examples 9 and 10), integrate directly instead.

steps: No real root and \(v(0) = 3 > 0\), so \(v > 0\) always: never at rest

blocks.prompt: 16 A particle has acceleration \(a(t) = 2\cos t\). It starts from rest at \(x = 1\) when \(t = 0\). Find \(v(t)\) and \(x(t)\), and the velocity and position at \(t = \frac{\pi}{2}\) and at \(t = \pi\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Integrate twice; remember \(\cos 0 = 1\) when fixing the second constant.

book_ref.quote: Writing \(\int \sin t\,dt = \cos t\) instead of \(-\cos t\).

blocks.prompt: 17 The acceleration of a particle is \(a(t) = \dfrac{4}{(t + 1)^{3}}\) m/s\(^{2}\) for \(t \ge 0\). It starts from rest at the origin. Find \(v(t)\), \(x(t)\) and the velocity and position at \(t = 1\) s. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Write \(a\) as \(4(t + 1)^{-3}\) and use the power rule twice.

book_ref.quote: fixing each constant from an initial condition

blocks.prompt: 18 A ball is thrown vertically upward from the ground with \(29.4\) m/s. Find (i) the maximum height (ii) the time to return to the ground (iii) the times at which it is \(24.5\) m above the ground. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Upward motion: \(a = -g\). At the top \(v = 0\). A given height is reached twice, once going up and once coming down.

book_ref.quote: the motion is called free fall or free vertical motion

steps: Time to the top: \(0 = 29.4 - 9.8t \Rightarrow t = 3\) s
Back to the ground: \(0 = 29.4t - 4.9t^{2} \Rightarrow t = 6\) s
\((t - 1)(t - 5) = 0 \Rightarrow t = 1\) s (going up) and \(t = 5\) s (coming down)

blocks.prompt: 19 A ball is dropped from the top of a tower \(49\) m high. At the same instant another ball is thrown vertically upward from the foot of the tower with \(24.5\) m/s. Find when and at what height above the ground they meet. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Write each ball's height above the ground at time \(t\) and set them equal.

book_ref.quote: The equations of motion for constant acceleration can also be used in vertical motion

steps: Check: rising ball \(24.5(2) - 19.6 = 29.4\) m; its velocity \(24.5 - 19.6 = 4.9 > 0\) (still going up)
blocks.final_answer: They meet after \(2\) s at \(29.4\) m above the ground.

blocks.prompt: 20 A stone is thrown vertically downward with \(4.9\) m/s from the top of a cliff \(58.8\) m high. Find the time it takes to reach the ground and its velocity on impact. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Downward motion: \(a = g\). Solve the quadratic for \(t\), keep the positive root.

book_ref.quote: If the particle moves downward, it accelerates toward the ground at the rate

blocks.prompt: 21 A ball is thrown vertically upward with \(9.8\) m/s from the top of a building \(39.2\) m high and falls to the ground beside it. Find (i) the greatest height of the ball above the ground (ii) the time it takes to reach the ground (iii) its speed on reaching the ground. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Take upward as positive throughout (\(a = -g\)); the ground is then at \(x = -39.2\) m from the roof.

book_ref.quote: Use the equations of motion with

steps: Rise above the roof: \(\dfrac{u^{2}}{2g} = \dfrac{9.8^{2}}{19.6} = 4.9\) m; greatest height \(= 39.2 + 4.9 = 44.1\) m
